children: Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) plans to temporarily discontinue 265 weekly international departures (one third of the total) from October 26 as a part of its wider plan to redevelop terminal 1 and push traffic to Navi Mumbai.
MIAL informed 46 airlines about planned reduction in slots on Thursday listing exactly the number of flights each airlines would lose.
Airlines have been asked to inform the airport by October 6 the specific departure slots they can surrender.
Airlines, however, are resisting the plan calling it forced relocation and have sought Civil Aviation Ministry’s intervention.

As per list circulated by the airport there are 770 weekly international departure slots at Mumbai’s terminal 2. IndiGo has highest number of slots (224) followed by Air India (100) and Akasa Air (32).
As per MIAL’s proposal 74 slots belonging to IndiGo and 33 slots belonging to Air India would be temporarily discontinued if the proposal goes through. Akasa Air stands to lose 11 weekly slots.

Similarly, among foreign carriers, Emirates and Etihad have highest number of departures each,  followed by British Airways. While Emirates flies 35 times a week, Etihad and British Airways operate 28 and 21 flights respectively. As per the MIAL proposal, ten slots, each of Emirates and Etihad would be temporarily discontinued while seven slots of British Airways would get reduced.

International Air Transport Association has said airlines plan schedules months in advance and any significant changes must be communicated sufficiently early to avoid disruption. The airline body has also called for consultation before cut in schedules.
Air France-KLM on Wednesday said splitting flights between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai is not a practical oprion.

On its part MIAL in its October 1 letter said airlines were called for stakeholder meeting on September 16. “A number of airline partners chose not to participate in the meeting. MIAL, nevertheless remains committed to continued stakeholder engagement and reiterates that the development programme and implementation timelines remain unchanged,” it said.
Mumbai airport will undertake phased redevelopment of its terminal 1 starting January 2027. As a consequence one third of domestic flights from T1 are planned to T2 from October 26.

title: Mumbai airport plans to discontinue 265 international flights from October 26, airlines opposed move
